verdict: Creating a private OAuth app for a single workspace is straightforward, with clear documentation for required fields and manifest options. Making an app public or an agent available to other workspaces introduces a submission/approval process and potentially requires a paid Linear plan for the approval feature. Rate limits are clearly defined.
time: Working time (estimate, not from docs): about 1-2 hours for initial setup and configuration. Approval wait time for public apps is not documented.
effort: Moderate developer effort for setup and configuration, with additional steps for public app submission and potential review.

requirements.text: A dedicated workspace is recommended for managing the OAuth2 Application.
The `display.description` field must be a short, user-facing description (max 1000 characters).
The `display.iconUrl` field must be an absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL for the application icon (recommendation: 256x256px).
The `developer.name` field is required for complete setup (min 2, max 80 characters).
The `oauth.client_name` field is required for complete setup (min 2, max 80 characters, must not contain 'Linear', 'http://', or 'https://').
The `oauth.client_uri` field is required for complete setup (absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL).
The `oauth.redirect_uris` field is required for complete setup (one or more absolute HTTP/HTTPS URLs, repeatable, min 1, max 32, values must be unique).
The `oauth.grant_types` field must include `authorization_code` (always required) and can optionally include `client_credentials` (repeatable).
If `webhook.url` is set, it must be an absolute HTTPS URL and cannot be a loopback, private-network, or `linear.app` host.
If `webhook.url` is set, `webhook.resourceTypes` must specify at least one resource type (repeatable, values must be unique).
For agents, enabling webhooks and selecting 'Agent session events' is required.
Integrations using the `actor=app` mode cannot request the `admin` scope.

blockers.text: To make an agent available to other workspaces, it must be submitted to Linear's integration directory for approval.
Third-party app approvals, which allow admins to review and approve apps before installation, are available only on paid Linear plans.
Calls to the GraphQL API are rate-limited to 5,000 requests per User (or App User) per 1 hour for OAuth Apps.
GraphQL API calls have a complexity limit of 2,000,000 points per User (or App User) per 1 hour, with a maximum complexity of 10,000 points for a single query.
Webhooks have quotas limiting them to 30 per team and 50 per workspace.

steps: Create a dedicated workspace for the OAuth2 Application (recommended).
Navigate to the OAuth application creation form.
Fill in required application details such as display name, description, icon URL, developer name, client URI, and redirect URIs.
Specify the required OAuth grant types, ensuring `authorization_code` is included.
Define desired scopes for the application's access.
Configure webhook settings if needed, providing a HTTPS URL and selecting resource types.
For public apps or agents, submit the application to Linear's integration directory for review and approval.
agent: Draft the OAuth application manifest or URL parameters with required fields and scopes.
Generate example code for the OAuth flow based on the specified grant types and redirect URIs.
Test the OAuth flow against a developer-owned Linear account to verify token exchange and API access.
you: Create a Linear account and a dedicated workspace for app development.
Provide the legal homepage/documentation URL (`oauth.client_uri`) and privacy policy URL (if applicable, though not explicitly required in notes).
Review and approve the drafted application details, scopes, and webhook configurations.
If making the app public or an agent, submit it to Linear's integration directory and potentially ensure the workspace is on a paid plan for the approval feature.
uncertain: Security assessments are not stated as a requirement for app approval.
